annotation.title_clean: Responsible AI #AIFORALL Part 1 – Principles for Responsible AI
annotation.title_en: Responsible AI #AIFORALL Part 1 – Principles for Responsible AI
annotation.authors_or_issuer: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), Government of India
annotation.summary_en: NITI Aayog's February 2021 approach paper sets out seven principles for responsible AI in India, grounded in constitutional fundamental rights. It reviews system and societal risks (opacity, bias, accountability, privacy, security, jobs), global regulatory approaches, and includes a self-assessment guide. Enforcement is deferred to Part 2. Autonomous vehicles appear only as a case example.
key_provisions_or_claims: Seven principles: safety and reliability, equality, inclusivity and non-discrimination, privacy and security, transparency, accountability, protection of positive human values
Principles derived from the Indian Constitution (Articles 14, 15, 16, 21)
Calls for a graded risk-based approach balancing soft governance and sector-specific regulation
Appendix self-assessment guide covering the AI lifecycle, ethics committees and grievance redressal
Enforcement mechanisms deferred to Part 2; India lacks overarching AI law
